q: The word 'computer' is rooted in which Latin word meaning 'to calculate or reckon'?
explain: Computer comes from compute, which traces back to the Latin computare. Originally a 'computer' was a person who did calculations.

q: Who is widely credited with developing the slide rule in the 1620s?
explain: William Oughtred is credited with the slide rule, which uses movable logarithmic scales. John Napier is linked with the numbered rods called Napier's Bones.

q: Among the abacus, Pascaline, Napier's Bones and Difference Engine, which is the earliest calculating aid?
explain: The abacus is an ancient manual aid, far older than Napier's Bones (1617), the Pascaline (1642) or Babbage's Difference Engine.

q: Blaise Pascal's Pascaline, built in 1642 with interconnected wheels and gears, mainly performed which operations?
explain: The Pascaline was designed for addition and subtraction. Multiplication and division came with Leibniz's Stepped Reckoner.

q: Which statement about Leibniz's Stepped Reckoner is correct?
options: It used a stepped drum and could add, subtract, multiply and divide
It was the first machine to be programmed with punched cards
It could only add and subtract, exactly like the Pascaline
It was an electronic machine built with vacuum tubes
explain: Leibniz's stepped drum and gears handled all four basic operations, going beyond Pascal's machine. It was purely mechanical.

q: In Babbage's Analytical Engine, which part held numbers and intermediate results, much like modern memory?
explain: The Store kept numbers and intermediate results, while the Mill did the arithmetic processing, like a modern ALU.

q: From which device did Babbage adapt the punched-card idea for programming the Analytical Engine?
explain: The Jacquard loom was already controlled by punched cards, and Babbage borrowed the idea for the Analytical Engine.

q: Who published extensive notes on the Analytical Engine in 1843, including an early computer program, and is widely called the first computer programmer?
explain: Ada Lovelace studied Babbage's Analytical Engine and published notes with an early program in 1843. Hollerith worked on punched-card census tabulation instead.

q: Which machine first successfully ran a program stored in electronic memory, on 21 June 1948?
explain: The Manchester Baby ran a stored program in electronic read-write memory in June 1948. ENIAC was general-purpose electronic but not originally stored-program, and Mark I was electromechanical.

q: Harvard Mark I, which began operating at Harvard in 1944, is best described as
options: a purely mechanical machine designed by Babbage
an electromechanical computer built by IBM engineers
explain: Howard Aiken conceived Mark I and IBM engineers built it as an electromechanical machine, so it does not belong with the vacuum-tube electronic computers.

q: What is the full form of EDSAC, the early practical stored-program computer of 1949?
explain: EDSAC stands for Electronic Delay Storage Automatic Calculator. EDVAC, by contrast, is Electronic Discrete Variable Automatic Computer.

q: John von Neumann's 1945 report on EDVAC is closely linked with which concept?
explain: The report helped explain and spread the stored-program idea, where instructions and data sit together in memory. Leibniz is the one tied to binary arithmetic.

q: In which year did IBM introduce its Personal Computer, Model 5150?
explain: IBM launched the PC Model 5150 on 12 August 1981. Apple II was 1977 and Apple I was 1976.

q: Which of these is recognised as the first commercially available single-chip microprocessor?
explain: Intel introduced the 4004 in 1971. Kenbak-1 of the same year is credited as the first commercial personal computer, not a microprocessor.

q: Who designed the Apple I, introduced in 1976?
explain: Steve Wozniak designed the Apple I, while Steve Jobs helped establish the early business.

q: Which statement about the Apple II (1977) is correct?
options: It was the first commercially available personal computer
It was launched by IBM in 1981
It was an influential early mass-market personal computer
It was the first single-chip microprocessor
explain: Apple II was an influential early mass-market PC, but the Kenbak-1 of 1971 is widely credited as the first commercially available personal computer.

q: Who is commonly called the Father of Artificial Intelligence and coined the term 'artificial intelligence' in 1955?
explain: John McCarthy used the term in 1955 for the proposed 1956 Dartmouth meeting. Alan Turing is called the Father of Modern Computer Science.

q: What does the Turing Test, proposed in 1950, examine?
options: How fast a computer can process data
Whether a machine can show human-like conversational behaviour
How much memory a computer needs to run programs
Whether a computer can store a program in memory
explain: A human evaluator chats by text and tries to tell a machine from a person. It looks at conversational behaviour, not every aspect of intelligence.

q: Which statement about the World Wide Web and the Internet is correct?
options: The Web is a system that runs over the Internet, and the two are not the same thing
The Web and the Internet are exactly the same thing
The Internet was invented by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN in 1989
The Web is the technical foundation known as TCP/IP
explain: Berners-Lee invented the Web in 1989 on top of the Internet. The Internet's technical foundation is TCP/IP, designed by Cerf and Kahn.

q: Who built the first working integrated circuit at Texas Instruments in 1958?
explain: Jack Kilby demonstrated the first working IC in 1958. Robert Noyce independently developed a practical silicon IC in 1959, so both share credit.

q: TCP/IP, the technical foundation of Internet communication, was co-designed by Vint Cerf and whom?
explain: Vint Cerf and Robert 'Bob' Kahn co-designed TCP/IP. Berners-Lee is credited with the World Wide Web instead.

q: Which of the following is NOT a programming language?
explain: UNIX is an operating system created at Bell Labs. Python, Java and PHP are programming languages.

q: Who created the Linux kernel, first released in 1991?
explain: Linus Torvalds created the Linux kernel. Ritchie created C, Thompson worked on UNIX, and Gosling designed Java.

q: Arattai, an Indian instant messaging app, was created by which company?
explain: Arattai comes from Zoho Corporation, whose co-founder is Sridhar Vembu. It had a soft launch in 2021.

q: Instagram was co-founded by Kevin Systrom and
explain: Instagram's co-founders are Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger. Koum and Acton founded WhatsApp, and Spiegel co-founded Snapchat.

q: The QWERTY keyboard layout takes its name from
options: the first six letters of the top-left letter row
the six most frequently used English letters
the first six keys of the numeric keypad
explain: QWERTY names the first six letters of the upper-left letter row, a layout developed from the Sholes typewriter.

q: Which of the following is a modifier key rather than a toggle key?
explain: Shift changes the action of another key when pressed with it. Caps Lock, Num Lock and Scroll Lock are toggle keys that switch a state.

q: How did the first mouse prototype built by Bill English in 1964 detect movement?
explain: The wooden prototype had two perpendicular wheels. The ball came with later mechanical mice and optical sensors with modern ones.

q: ENIAC, an early vacuum-tube computer, used roughly how many vacuum tubes (rounded)?
explain: University of Pennsylvania records give 17,468 tubes, commonly rounded to about 18,000.

q: Which computer generation is associated with the introduction of microprocessors?
explain: Microprocessors and increasingly dense LSI/VLSI circuits mark the fourth generation. The third used ICs and the fifth is linked with AI.

q: Which statement about VLSI and ULSI is correct?
options: They are separate technologies that replaced the integrated circuit
They are types of vacuum tube
They describe levels of integration within integrated circuits
They are generations of programming languages
explain: VLSI and ULSI describe how densely transistors are packed on an IC; they do not replace the IC concept.

q: IBM 650 is a well-known example of a computer that used which memory technology?
explain: The IBM 650 used magnetic-drum memory, a rotating cylinder with a magnetic surface. Not all first-generation computers used the same memory.

q: Which time unit equals 10^-9 second?
explain: A nanosecond is 10^-9 s. Each step in the sequence ms, µs, ns, ps, fs is 1,000 times smaller than the last.

q: KIPS, associated with fifth-generation research, stands for
explain: KIPS means Knowledge Information Processing System, which uses knowledge and inference to solve problems. It is not an input/output device.

q: What does MIPS stand for as a measure of processor performance?
explain: MIPS is Millions of Instructions Per Second. Alone it cannot reliably compare different processor architectures.

q: In a second-generation-style assembly language, an assembler translates the symbolic instructions into what?
explain: Assembly uses symbolic mnemonics, and an assembler converts them into binary machine code (1GL).

q: Which statement about batch processing is correct?
options: It was used only in first-generation computers
It began in the 1950s and continued across generations
It needs the user to type each command and wait for a reply
It was invented after the graphical user interface
explain: Batch systems appeared in the 1950s (GM-NAA dates to 1956) and kept being used, so batch processing is not exclusive to the first generation.

q: Which approach has several cores or processing units working on parts of the same task at the same time?
explain: Parallel processing is concurrent computation on multiple units. Distributed computing instead coordinates separate connected computers.

q: Which statement about a qubit is correct?
options: It can be prepared in state 0, state 1 or a superposition of both
It always holds both 0 and 1, so quantum computers are faster at every task
It is just another name for a classical bit
It is measured as a continuous value between 0 and 1
explain: A qubit can be in 0, 1 or a superposition, but measuring it gives 0 or 1. 'Both at once' is only a shorthand, and quantum computers are not faster for every task.

q: Which term refers to connected physical devices, such as sensors and smart devices, that collect or exchange data?
explain: IoT (Internet of Things) covers connected physical devices. A LAN or WAN is a network type, and cloud computing delivers services over a network.
